title: India Seal ODI Series 3-1 in New Zealand, Hold No. 1 Ranking
excerpt: Defending just 209 at Bay Oval, India's pace attack triggered a New Zealand collapse from 64 for 1 to 119 for 6, sealing a 22-run win and a nine-point lead at the top of the ICC ODI rankings.
body:
• India beat New Zealand by 22 runs in the fifth ODI at Bay Oval, Mount Maunganui, defending 209 to seal the five-match series 3-1.
  • New Zealand cruised to 64 for 1 chasing 210, then lost five wickets for 55 runs; Arshdeep Singh took 3 for 30 and Axar Patel scored 46 and took two wickets.
  • India stay No. 1 in the ICC ODI rankings on 116 points, nine clear of New Zealand on 107.
  • The two teams next meet in a two-Test series beginning November 19.

India defended a modest 209 to beat New Zealand by 22 runs in the fifth and final one-day international at Bay Oval, Mount Maunganui, on Sunday, sealing the five-match series 3-1 and consolidating their position at the top of the ICC ODI rankings.

Put in to bat, India were bowled out for 209 in 42.1 overs. New Zealand reached 64 for 1 in reply and looked in control of the chase, before India's pace attack sparked a collapse of five wickets for 55 runs. The hosts were eventually dismissed for 187 in 48.1 overs, according to Reuters.

How the match turned

India's batting never settled. Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli and Ruturaj Gaikwad were all dismissed inside nine overs, and it took a 52-run partnership between Axar Patel and Shreyas Iyer (22) to steady the innings. Patel and Ishan Kishan scored 46 apiece — the only Indian batters to pass 25 — and Naman Dhir added a late 22. Mitchell Santner took 3 for 47 and Jacob Duffy 3 for 60 for New Zealand, with Matthew Fisher claiming two wickets.

The chase followed the opposite script. Openers Will Young and Nick Kelly put New Zealand on course before Yash Thakur built pressure with a disciplined spell and Mohammed Siraj and Arshdeep Singh struck at regular intervals as the hosts slumped from 64 for 1 to 119 for 6. Dean Foxcroft top-scored with 31 off 42 balls before Thakur removed him for his maiden ODI wicket. Santner's 24 off 31 offered late resistance, but India's bowlers wrapped up the tail. Arshdeep finished with 3 for 30 from his 10 overs, while Siraj and Patel took two wickets each.

"The young pace attack delivered what they promised."

— Fan reaction reported by Sportskeeda after the series win

What it means

Both teams held their positions in the updated ICC men's ODI team rankings, but India gained a rating point and New Zealand lost one, stretching the gap at the top to nine points: India on 116, New Zealand on 107, with South Africa and Pakistan next on 104, according to Wisden. India, who had also won the preceding T20 series 3-2, will carry the No. 1 ranking into three further ODIs against Sri Lanka later this year.

The result is India's first ODI series win in New Zealand since 2019 and ends the hosts' run of 11 unbeaten home ODI series, Sportskeeda reported. India achieved it short-handed: captain Shubman Gill and KL Rahul missed the last two ODIs, and Jasprit Bumrah was rested for the entire series, Wisden noted. It was also a recovery from the previous match, where New Zealand had beaten India by 244 runs to keep the series alive.

What's next

India and New Zealand next meet in a two-Test series beginning on November 19, Reuters reported. India then close out their ODI year with three matches against Sri Lanka, entering the new year as the top-ranked side in the 50-over format.
